records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G2 R2 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Nītimati
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M2 P D3 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D3 P M2 G2 R2 S
records.mood: gentle, lesser-performed
records.notes: Occasional concert presence; performed mainly via specific compositions.

records.name: Kāntāmaṇi
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D1 N1 S
records.avarohana: S N1 D1 P M2 G3 R2 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Ṛṣabhapriyā
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M2 G3 R2 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Laṭāṅgi
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R2 S
records.mood: bright, assertive
records.notes: Reasonably popular in modern concerts; source of a few janyas.

records.name: Vācaspati
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
records.mood: stately, contemplative
records.notes: Fairly popular in concerts; do not confuse with Kalyani/Mechakalyani (65), which replaces shuddha madhyamam with prati madhyamam and shifts the whole color to auspicious/evening.

records.name: Kalyāṇi
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R2 S
records.mood: auspicious, expansive; the classic evening raga
records.notes: Common name simply 'Kalyāṇi' (also 'Mechakalyani' to distinguish from Hindustani-influenced variants); equivalent scale to the Western lydian-flavoured major-with-sharp-4; one of the most popular ragas in all Carnatic music, huge janya family (Poorvikalyani via M1 sibling relationship is a separate mela, not a janya).

records.name: Citrāmbari
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M2 P D3 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D3 P M2 G3 R2 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Sucaritra
records.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D1 N1 S
records.avarohana: S N1 D1 P M2 G3 R3 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Jyōtisvarūpiṇi
records.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M2 G3 R3 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Dhātuvardhini
records.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R3 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Nāsikābhūṣaṇi
records.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M2 G3 R3 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Kōsalam
records.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D2 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M2 G3 R3 S
records.mood: gentle, lesser-performed
records.notes: Occasional concert presence via specific compositions.

records.name: Rasikapriyā
records.arohana: S R3 G3 M2 P D3 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D3 P M2 G3 R3 S
records.mood: a scale of the 72-mela system; character depends on rendering, since it has little independent concert tradition
records.notes: One of the 72 melakartas. Known chiefly as a scale exercise and through the systematic 'melakarta' composition sets (e.g. by Koteeswara Iyer / Maha Vaidyanatha Sivan) rather than a large independent concert repertoire.

records.name: Ābhēri
records.arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: Soft, pleading, deeply melodic — the rāga of Nagumōmu Galavāni.
records.notes: Audava ascent, sampūrṇa descent. Some paṭhāntarams sing the descent with D1 (making it closer to Karnāṭaka Dēvagāndhāri); the D2 version given here is the one commonly heard today.

records.name: Abhōgī
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 S
records.avarohana: S D2 M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: sweet, gently pensive; a favorite for varnams and swarajatis
records.notes: Pentatonic — omits panchamam and nishadam entirely. Very close in feel to Hindustani Abhogi; easy to confuse with Madhyamavati (which keeps P, N2, drops G) or Sriranjani (which keeps N, drops P).

records.name: Ānandabhairavi
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: tender, romantic, a little wistful; extremely popular rakti raga
records.notes: Bhashanga raga: uses antara gandharam (G3) and kakali nishadam (N3) as anya (borrowed) swaras against its Natabhairavi (R2 G2 ... D1 N2) base — many performers realize the gandharam as a vakra oscillation between G2 and G3. Characteristic phrase 'S G3 R2 S' / 'N3 D2 P'. One of the oldest and most beloved rakti ragas.

records.name: Āndōḷikā
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 R2 S
records.mood: Gently rocking — the name means "swing", and the melodic motion earns it.
records.notes: Gāndhāra is dropped in both directions; dhaivata appears only in descent. Rāgasudhārasa is the one everyone learns.

records.name: Ārabhi
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: bright, brisk, auspicious; common at the start of a concert or a mangalam
records.notes: Audava (5-note) ascent skipping G and N, sampurna descent. Easily confused with Bilahari, which also skips notes ascending but includes G3 there; Arabhi's ascent has no G at all.

records.name: Āṭhāṇa
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: vigorous, martial, celebratory
records.notes: Ascent skips gandharam (audava-like); gandharam (G3) enters only in descent, often via a vakra turn near the tara shadja. Famous vehicle: Tyagaraja's 'Ela ni daya radu'.

records.name: Bahudāri
records.arohana: S G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G3 S
records.mood: Crisp and cheerful; dhaivata appears going up but not coming down.
records.notes: The asymmetry — D2 in the ārōhaṇa, absent in the avarōhaṇa — is what separates Bahudāri from its neighbours. Brōva Bhāramā is the standard.

records.name: Bēgaḍa
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: warm, festive, richly ornamented
records.notes: Known for the characteristic vakra phrase 'G3 R2 S N2. S' descending to the lower shadja; heavily used for javalis and tukkadas as well as substantial kritis.

records.name: Bhairavi
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: grand, deeply moving, all-encompassing; one of the great rakti ragas
records.notes: Bhashanga raga: in addition to the sampurna scale shown, advanced performers weave in chatushruti dhaivatam (D2) and kakali nishadam (N3) as anya swaras in the famous descending phrase 'S N3 D2 N2 D1 P'. One of the ghanaraga-adjacent, most revered ragas in the repertoire; do not confuse with the Hindustani Bhairavi, which is a different scale entirely (closer to Carnatic Hanumatodi).

records.name: Bilahari
records.arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: bright, cheerful, auspicious morning raga
records.notes: Audava ascent skipping madhyamam and nishadam; sampurna descent. Common at concert openings and for light, joyous compositions.

records.name: Darbār
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: majestic, grave, courtly
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and dhaivatam (audava); gandharam and dhaivatam appear only in a vakra descent. Adapted into Carnatic practice from the Hindustani darbari tradition; distinguish from Bhairavi and Ritigaula which share the same parent notes.

records.name: Dēvagāndhāri
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: gentle, contemplative, slightly plaintive
records.notes: Bhashanga raga: borrows kaisiki nishadam (N2) in descent, foreign to parent Sankarabharanam (which has N3). Ascent typically omits gandharam and nishadam.

records.name: Dēvamanōhari
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: sweet and unhurried, close cousin of Mohanam/Kambhoji-family ragas
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and nishadam; both appear in the sampurna descent. Less common than its melodic cousins Devagandhari and Kambhoji — do not conflate the three.

records.name: Dhanyāsi
records.arohana: S G2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: poignant, tender, devotional
records.notes: Audava ascent (no rishabham, no dhaivatam); rishabham (R2) is added only in the shadava descent, its most distinctive feature. Very popular for kritis and as a raga-alapana vehicle; not to be confused with Hindustani Dhani, which is a different scale.

records.name: Gauḷa
records.arohana: S R1 M1 P N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 P M1 R1 G3 M1 R1 S
records.mood: One of the five ghana rāgas — weighty, ancient, built for tānam.
records.notes: A ghana rāga: the crooked descent through M1 R1 G3 M1 R1 is the rāga, not decoration. Carries Dudukugala Nannē, the second Pañcaratna.

records.name: Haṁsadhvani
records.arohana: S R2 G3 P N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 P G3 R2 S
records.mood: bright, regal, invocatory
records.notes: Pentatonic both ways, omits madhyamam and dhaivatam. Extremely popular concert-opener and for invocations of Ganesha; Dikshitar's 'Vatapi Ganapatim' is the best-known vehicle.

records.name: Haṃsanādaṃ
records.arohana: S R2 M2 P N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 P M2 R2 S
records.mood: Bright and springy — a prati-madhyama pentatonic with real forward drive.
records.notes: Only five notes, all of them strong: the leap S R2 M2 and the N3 on the way down are the whole rāga. Bantu Rīti Kolu lives here.

records.name: Hindōḷaṃ
records.arohana: S G2 M1 D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 M1 G2 S
records.mood: Grave and self-contained; no rishabha, no panchama.
records.notes: Both R and P are dropped, which is what gives Hindōḷaṃ its still, unhurried feel. Sāmaja Vara Gamana is the textbook example.

records.name: Jaganmōhini
records.arohana: S G3 M1 P N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 P M1 G3 S
records.mood: Sweet and compact — no rishabha, no dhaivata.
records.notes: A symmetric pentatonic in the Māyāmāḷavagauḷa family. Śōbhillu Saptasvara is the kṛti students meet first.

records.name: Jayantasēna
records.arohana: S G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: Plaintive and questioning, close to Ābhēri but for the dhaivata in ascent.
records.notes: Used for essentially one kriti — Marugēlarā — so the rāga and the composition are learnt together. The D2 in the ārōhaṇa is what keeps it distinct from Ābhēri.

records.name: Kāmbhōji
records.arohana: S R2 G3 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: majestic, expansive, devotional; considered one of the greatest rakti ragas
records.notes: Ascent typically omits nishadam; the kaisiki nishadam (N2) governs the descent, and shuddha nishadam (N1) is occasionally touched as a bhashanga anya swara in specific gamaka-laden phrases (e.g. 'S N1 D P'). One of the ghana-panchaka-adjacent rakti ragas, central to Tyagaraja's output (e.g. 'O Rangasayee').

records.name: Kānaḍā
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 M1 R2 S
records.mood: Coiling and ornamented; almost impossible to sing straight.
records.notes: Heavily vakra in both directions — the phrase M1 G2 M1 R2 in descent and the skipped panchama in ascent are the rāga. Nearly always taught by imitation rather than from the scale.

records.name: Kāpi
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 N2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: tender, folksy, romantic; a favorite for tukkadas and javalis
records.notes: Complex bhashanga raga: uses both kaisiki (N2) and kakali (N3) nishadam and admits vakra turns freely; treat the notation above as a simplified skeleton — real practice leans heavily on gamaka and phrase-memory rather than a fixed scale. Very popular in the concert 'tukkada' segment.

records.name: Kāpī Nārāyaṇi
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: Stately and a little grand; unrelated to the lighter Kāpi despite the name.
records.notes: Gāndhāra is absent going up and present coming down. Do not confuse it with Kāpi, which is a different, bhāṣāṅga rāga.

records.name: Kēdāragauḷa
records.arohana: S G2 R2 G2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: solid, upright, devotional
records.notes: Ascent omits dhaivatam and is characteristically vakra around the gandharam ('G2 R2 G2 M1'). Not the same raga as the Hindustani Kedar. Vehicle for Tyagaraja's 'Sri Ganapatini'.

records.name: Khamās
records.arohana: S M1 G3 M1 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: Warm, lilting, at home in lighter concert slots.
records.notes: Rishabha is skipped in the ascent and the phrase M1 G3 M1 is characteristic. N3 appears as a bhāṣāṅga touch in some phrases.

records.name: Kuntaḷavarāḷi
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 P M1 R2 S
records.mood: brisk, folk-flavored, unusual
records.notes: Pentatonic, omits gandharam and dhaivatam; its kakali nishadam (N3) is foreign to the parent Kharaharapriya (which has N2), making it technically bhashanga. Used for fast, playful compositions.

records.name: Lalita
records.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 D1 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D1 M2 G3 R1 S
records.mood: serene, contemplative; a traditional early-morning raga
records.notes: Omits panchamam entirely (one of the few common panchama-varjya ragas) while using prati madhyamam (M2). Do not confuse with the unrelated raga 'Lalitha Panchamam', which restores panchamam and shifts the color considerably.

records.name: Madhyamāvati
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 P M1 R2 S
records.mood: cheerful, clear, auspicious; standard raga for tanam and concert openers
records.notes: Pentatonic both ways, omits gandharam and dhaivatam entirely. One of the most commonly taught and performed audava ragas; frequently the very first raga used for alapana practice.

records.name: Malayamārutaṃ
records.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M2 G3 R1 S
records.mood: Fresh and breezy — the name means "mountain breeze".
records.notes: A straight sampūrṇa janya of Rāmapriya; the R1 against M2 is what gives it its distinctive lift.

records.name: Mōhanam
records.arohana: S R2 G3 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S D2 P G3 R2 S
records.mood: joyous, radiant, universally loved
records.notes: Pure pentatonic (major-scale-like), omits madhyamam and nishadam entirely; identical note-set to the widely known 'major pentatonic'. Extremely popular across genres; distinguish from Hamsadhvani (which has nishadam, not dhaivatam).

records.name: Mukhāri
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D1 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: deeply devotional, tinged with pathos; traditionally sung post-dawn
records.notes: Bhashanga raga: its shuddha dhaivatam (D1) is foreign to the parent Kharaharapriya (which has D2), giving Mukhari its distinctive weight. Gandharam appears mainly in descent.

records.name: Naṭa
records.arohana: S R1 M1 P D2 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R1 S
records.mood: vigorous, martial, celebratory; traditionally used to open concerts and processions
records.notes: Bhashanga raga: uses shuddha rishabham (R1) in place of Sankarabharanam's chatushruti rishabham (R2); gandharam appears only in a vakra descent. Do not confuse with mela 36 'Chalanata', an unrelated melakarta with a similar name.

records.name: Nāyaki
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P M1 D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: deep, meditative; a late-night/ghana-adjacent raga favored for RTP
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and is vakra around the madhyamam ('M1 P M1 D2'); gandharam (G2) appears only in descent. Closely related to Kapi and Sahana but simpler and without kakali nishadam.

records.name: Nīlāmbari
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: slow, hushed, tender — the classic lullaby raga
records.notes: Rendered with heavy gamaka and vakra, meandering phrases at a very slow tempo; traditionally used for lullabies ('jo achyutananda'-type songs) and to close a concert gently.

records.name: Punnāgavarāḷi
records.arohana: S G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R1 S
records.mood: intense, austere, associated with pathos and penance
records.notes: Ascent omits rishabham; rishabham (R1) appears only in descent. Traditionally associated with grief/separation (viraha) themes.

records.name: Pūrvikalyāṇi
records.arohana: S R1 G3 M2 P D1 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G3 R1 S
records.mood: serene, expansive, devotional; a favored evening raga
records.notes: Sampurna both ways, sharing its parent's full note-set. Easily confused by name with Kalyani/Mechakalyani (mela 65) — Poorvikalyani instead uses shuddha rishabham (R1) and shuddha dhaivatam (D1), giving it a very different, more subdued color.

records.name: Rītigauḷa
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: grave, searching; a vivadi-flavored ghana-adjacent raga
records.notes: Ascent omits panchamam, which is added only, vakra-style, in descent ('D1 P M1'). Vehicle for Tyagaraja's 'Nannu Vidachi Kadala'.

records.name: Sahāna
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P M1 D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: sweet, lingering, richly ornamented
records.notes: Ascent is vakra around the madhyamam ('M1 P M1 D2'); a favorite raga for extended alapana and RTP, known for heavy gamaka usage on gandharam and nishadam.

records.name: Sāramati
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 P D1 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D1 M1 G2 S
records.mood: Contemplative and inward; the descent drops P and R entirely.
records.notes: Sampūrṇa ascent against a four-note descent, which is unusual and gives the rāga its sighing quality. Mōkṣamu Galadā is the definitive kṛti.

records.name: Sāraṅga
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 P M1 R2 G2 R2 S
records.mood: playful, bright, forenoon raga
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and dhaivatam; gandharam re-enters only via a vakra turn at the very end of the descent ('R2 G2 R2 S'), dhaivatam is generally avoided altogether. Adapted from a Hindustani-influenced tradition into Carnatic practice.

records.name: Saurāṣṭraṃ
records.arohana: S R1 G3 M1 P D2 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 P M1 G3 R1 S
records.mood: Auspicious and processional; the traditional maṅgaḷam rāga.
records.notes: A bhāṣāṅga rāga: N2 appears as a foreign note in characteristic descending phrases, and the full avarōhaṇa is often sung vakra. The scale below is the pedagogical skeleton, not the whole rāga.

records.name: Sāvēri
records.arohana: S R1 M1 P D1 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M1 G3 R1 S
records.mood: solemn, devotional; traditionally sung in the morning
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and nishadam (audava); both appear in a full descent. A very old and revered raga, popular for tanam.

records.name: Śrī
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: grave, ceremonial; traditionally the raga used to close a concert
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and dhaivatam (audava); the descent is fully sampurna. By tradition often the last raga performed at a concert ('mangalam' association) and rendered at a slow, weighty tempo despite the sparse ascent.

records.name: Śrīrañjani
records.arohana: S R2 G2 M1 D2 N2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: sweet, buoyant, devotional
records.notes: Pentatonic both ways, omits panchamam entirely. Easily confused with Abhogi (which omits nishadam instead of panchamam) — remember Sriranjani keeps N2 and drops P.

records.name: Śuddha Baṅgāḷa
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: Plain-spoken and steady, close in feel to Śuddha Sāvēri with a softer gāndhāra.
records.notes: G2 appears only in the descent, which is the single feature that tells it apart from Śuddha Sāvēri.

records.name: Śuddhasāvēri
records.arohana: S R2 G2 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S D2 P G2 R2 S
records.mood: simple, open, folk-like; often used for beginner varnams and tillanas
records.notes: Pure pentatonic, omits madhyamam and nishadam entirely. Not to be confused with the parent-raga Saveri (mela 15), which despite the similar name has a completely different note-set.

records.name: Surati
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S D2 P M1 G2 R2 S
records.mood: lively, sweet, dance-like
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and nishadam; nishadam is generally avoided altogether while gandharam is confined to the descent. Rendered with characteristic vakra turns around panchamam and dhaivatam.

records.name: Varāḷi
records.arohana: S G1 R1 G1 M2 P D1 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D1 P M2 G1 R1 S
records.mood: Austere and slightly unsettling; a ghana rāga traditionally taught with caution.
records.notes: The vakra ārōhaṇa (S G1 R1 G1 …) is essential. Tradition holds that a guru does not teach Varāḷi directly to a student — it is picked up by listening. Carries Kanakana Rucirā, the fourth Pañcaratna.

records.name: Vasanta
records.arohana: S G3 M1 D2 N3 S
records.avarohana: S N3 D2 M1 G3 R1 S
records.mood: delicate, springtime, festive
records.notes: Classed here under the 17th mela (Sūryakāntam), whose D2 and N3 it actually uses; older texts list it under Māyāmāḷavagauḷa, which makes it bhāṣāṅga. Rishabha and panchama are both dropped.

records.name: Yadukulakāmbhōji
records.arohana: S R2 M1 P D2 S
records.avarohana: S N2 D2 P M1 G3 R2 S
records.mood: folk-flavored, bright, unpretentious
records.notes: Ascent omits gandharam and nishadam; gandharam (G3) and kaisiki nishadam (N2) appear only in descent. Distinguish carefully from Kambhoji itself, which is a closely related but distinct janya of the same parent mela.
